title: Make device projection replay and crash idempotent
description: The changed-fid roster optimization still materializes replayed device claims before filtering reconciliation. A stale lower-fid/rank-losing claim can overwrite the canonical projection, and a crash after root/index commit but before app materialization leaves the same inconsistency on retry. Make the read model generation-aware or otherwise ensure replays are canonical/no-op.
acceptance_criteria: A stale losing device claim cannot replace the canonical roster row; retry after commit-before-materialize repairs the app projection; ordinary device-authored writes still avoid a full roster rebuild; realistic regression tests cover both failure modes.
close_reason: App projections now carry a manifest-generation stamp, lagging projections rebuild before replay, and aligned replays materialize only new ids; crash and stale-loser regressions pass.

title: Make FsStore concurrent puts atomic
description: The chained-auth black-box suite exposed concurrent PUTs to the same FsStore key sharing p+'.tmp'. One thread renames that pathname and the other raises FileNotFoundError, returning HTTP 500. Use per-write unique temp files while preserving atomic os.replace and clean abandoned temps.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic concurrent-put regression makes both writers complete without error, leaves one complete value at the key, and leaves no temp files; the full suite passes.
close_reason: FsStore now uses unique same-directory temp files for atomic concurrent puts; deterministic race regression and black-box test pass; Codex and Claude Fable approved.

title: Reschedule sync after quarantine restoration
description: A walk can restore a locally quarantined fact only after its push set was computed, then cache the peer ETag against the new local root. Later 304 responses may return early forever, so the restored fact never reaches the peer and roots remain divergent.
acceptance_criteria: Restoring any quarantined fact invalidates or reschedules every peer walk cache for that workspace; add a realistic two-peer regression that restores after push-set calculation and proves a subsequent no-new-write walk converges; retain ordinary 304 pruning when no restoration occurs.
close_reason: Quarantine restoration now invalidates every workspace peer cache so the next unchanged walk republishes restored facts; realistic two-peer pull-then-follow-up-push regression passes.

title: Bind mint evaluation to committed canonical authority
description: A caller can present an independently valid stale closure that omits a committed conflicting authority winner. Evaluate mode currently canonicalizes only inside the caller-controlled pile, so a fact pruned from the workspace canonical set can still authorize a sync token.
acceptance_criteria: Evaluate mode compares presented need providers with committed canonical providers while preserving globals-blind durable validation and first-sync for genuinely new descendants; add a regression for a quarantined losing device chain and a positive fresh-delegation case; pass the canonical workspace view atomically from the mint seam.
close_reason: Committed canonical evaluation now checks semantic need compatibility, not provider-id equality: incompatible co-offer winners reject stale quarantined chains while honest diverged peers mint both ways and can converge.

title: Hoisting in production: settle-node closure placement (ρ→1); retire flat per-leaf closure
description: SIMPLIFY.md §2 ('optional settle hook = hoisting', hoist.py's _spans/_settle) + MULTILEVEL_PILE.md. Land hoisting in the PRODUCTION store/sync path as an engine capability on tree.py (808.2): factor each closure fact ONCE to its settle node (the LCA of the leaves needing it), so every root-to-node path is a closed set and full-sync download drops to one copy of each fact — ρ→1 vs the flat per-leaf-closure ρ≈3x measured. Replaces layout.py's per-leaf close(). Keep the two identities distinct: fp (in-range keys, the diff identity) vs oid (h(pile bytes), closure included, the fetch identity) — so hoisted closure copies stay out of the diff algebra. Range-sync becomes a flat shared-core tax (MULTILEVEL_PILE A.4-A.5; key order must be dep-aligned or it can lose to leaf-only piles for small pulls). Verify against the prototype measurements (bench_hoist, bench_hoist_sync, bench_order). SHARED-POOL BENEFIT: T_supp (yez.2/yez.10) reuses the SAME content-addressed settle-node closure pool as T_fact — one hoisted closure store across both trees. Status today: hoist.py is PROTOTYPE/bench-only (not in node/walk/kernel); this bead is its production landing, distinct from 808.3 which only deletes hoist._judge on the kernel side.

title: Make removal projection independent of membership materialization order
description: A valid removal can have an older timestamp than the target's membership fact. During canonical reprojection, close() may materialize the removal before the user row; removal's UPDATE then affects zero rows and the later user materialization inserts evicted=0. The same accepted fact set can therefore expose a non-evicted member after rebuild/reprojection even though the removal global is present. Resolve this with the suppression/remove-wins model rather than relying on projector order.
acceptance_criteria: Add a regression with an old-timestamp removal preceding target membership during reprojection; prove fresh projection, rebuild, and opposite arrival orders expose the same removed state; preserve stable validation and parallel drain; implement remove-wins through the global suppression design or another explicitly approved order-independent projection rule.

title: Property suite: E order-independence + rebuild equivalence (fold± ≡ fold over E)
description: SIMPLIFY.md §6. (a) E = V ∖ S order-independent: random pile partitions × delivery orders × batchings ⇒ same effective set (extends the history-independence test). (b) THE theorem: live fold-with-retractions over delivery order == clean fold over E in canonical order (rebuild computes S first from T_supp/root, zero retractions fire). (c) Contract extensions: deletion refs its target; suppression facts not themselves suppressible (S stays monotone); pump-twice = no change; pump crash/resume.
notes: Skeleton on branch simplify-skeleton: tests/test_eset.py (E order-independence, monotone S, verdicts never read S) + THE-theorem section of tests/test_pump.py (fold± over D == fold over E; rebuild fires zero retractions).

title: Projector contract: rows keyed by src, generic retraction, confluence fix
description: SIMPLIFY.md §5. AST-enforced contract: every projector row carries its producing src fid; handlers contain ZERO suppression logic; retraction is one generic pump op (DELETE … WHERE src=?) across the family's tables. Blessed discipline: insert-only rows keyed by src + views for aggregates (abelian later, LWW never). Fixes the removal/join confluence bug: removal.materialize's UPDATE members SET evicted=1 is delivery-order-dependent — replace with insert-only removals row + a view for the evicted display flag (member display data, not fact suppression; S never lives in app.db).
notes: Skeleton on branch simplify-skeleton: pump.retract + pump.tables_of stubs. Acceptance tests: contract section of tests/test_pump.py (src column, generic retraction, no suppression in handlers, removal/join confluence).

title: Mint = evaluate∘close: family grant hook, thin daemon.mint, root-riding globals
description: SIMPLIFY.md §4. mint(pile) = decode → evaluate(pile, anchor, globals ∪ {(now, now_ms())}) → seal(token(grant_of(pile))). Family owns policy via request.grant(f) → (pk, verb); daemon's hand-rolled tag/arity/expiry checks move into the family evaluate hook. Rule: exactly one DURABLE=False fact per mint pile. Stateless Worker/λ mint = GET root (anchor+globals ride the root node after the manifest drop, see .2) → evaluate → presign; the λ never builds app.db. Supplies the two-predicate frame (valid immutable/globals-blind; E = V ∖ S monotone-difference) + the gate-mask seam candidate (screen the WHOLE submitted closure against S at mint/ingress) to yez.9 / gxz — decision stays with yez.9.
notes: Skeleton on branch simplify-skeleton: tinyp2p/mint.py (mint/grant_of/screen/root_globals; two-predicate frame in the docstring; request-family hook contract). Acceptance tests named in tests/test_mint.py.

title: Delivery log + atomic cursor: log(seq, ±fid), exactly-once pump
description: SIMPLIFY.md §5. idx.db gains log(seq, ±fid): merge() appends +fid per newly admitted durable fact, −target per target of a newly admitted deletion (single-target now; yez.3's surfacing pass streams 1:N victims in later). Deletion refs its target ⇒ −t always follows +t. app.db gains cursors(ws, projector, seq); the pump applies rows and advances the cursor in ONE transaction — exactly-once replaces idempotence as the handler obligation. Consumer of yez.11's resolve_supp flag on the read-model side.
notes: Skeleton on branch simplify-skeleton: tinyp2p/pump.py (LOG_SCHEMA/CURSOR_SCHEMA, append_admitted/append_retracted/pump). Acceptance tests: exactly-once section of tests/test_pump.py.

title: One kernel loop: path scratchpad as a kernel capability; delete hoist._judge
description: SIMPLIFY.md §1, staging S2. hoist._judge/_insert/_pop is a copy-paste of the kernel VALIDATE loop. Move the push/pop verified-ancestor scratchpad (sqlite :memory:) into kernel.py as a capability; verify_once and drain share one judge. Then the sync walk carries the SAME scratchpad across consecutive ranges — closing the known catchup re-verify tax (shared verified set across ranges). Gate: hoist bench judge counts unchanged (judge-ops = |V| cold).
notes: Skeleton on branch simplify-skeleton: kernel.Scratchpad stub appended to tinyp2p/kernel.py (judge/context/pop), tree.verify signature. Acceptance tests: kernel-unification section of tests/test_engine.py (judge-ops == |V| cold, scratchpad across ranges, hoist._judge deleted).

title: shape.py: key fn / boundary / priority / cut tiers / fp as engine parameters
description: SIMPLIFY.md §1. Extract the pure shape layer every tree shares: key function (ts:fid for T_fact, suppkey||tag||ts:fid for T_supp), boundary(fid), treap priority, cut tiers (CUT/COLD_CUT/GUARD), and the fp (diff identity, in-range keys only) vs oid (storage identity, h(pile bytes)) split. No I/O, no policy. T_supp (yez.2) and the fat packing (jbg.1) become key-function/packing choices, not new modules.
notes: Skeleton: tinyp2p/shape.py on branch simplify-skeleton (Shape bundle, FACT instantiation, supp_shape() stub for yez.10; CUT/COLD_CUT/GUARD move here).
close_reason: Centralized canonical key parsing/formatting, cut tiers, boundary, priority, and fingerprints in pure shape.py; removed duplicates across layout/treap/hoist/walk/node and benches; 83-test suite and byte-identity benchmark green; Codex and Claude Fable approved.

title: tree.py: ONE build/fold/diff/merge recursion, sans-io, three packings
description: SIMPLIFY.md §0–§2. The one two-tree recursion with fetch/emit callbacks: build, fold (blind update), diff (pruned walk), merge (two-root tree-join). Packing parameter: F=2 binary (today's treap.py), F=∞ inlined (today's layout.py manifest), F≈32–256 fat nodes (jbg.1 target). EXECUTE jbg.1 AS THIS EXTRACTION — one rewrite, not two; jbg.2 = diff with a range-GET driver, jbg.4 = merge. Golden gates: byte-identity within packings across insert orders/batchings; identical leaf sets across packings; read-floor counters on dict drivers. Flag: anchor+globals move to the root node when the flat manifest drops (mint depends on this, .4).
notes: Skeleton on branch simplify-skeleton: tinyp2p/tree.py (View/Packing/Root, build/fold/diff/merge/verify, BINARY+FLAT+fat packings), tinyp2p/sync.py (thin initiator over tree.diff), store.RemoteStore stub. Acceptance tests named in tests/test_engine.py (golden gates, fold laws, read floor).

title: Simplify: one tree engine, one kernel, mint=evaluate, cursored pump
description: Plan: SIMPLIFY.md. The codebase contains ONE two-tree recursion written five times (treap.update, layout, walk, hoist.verify_once, rebuild) with two more copies scheduled (jbg.1 fat-node fold, yez T_supp walk). Extract the engine once — AS the fat-node rewrite — plus: one kernel loop (delete hoist._judge), mint = evaluate∘close (family grant hook), and read models as a cursored pure fold with generic retraction. Every bead names its SIMPLIFY.md section.
notes: Skeletons landed (2026-07-24): branch simplify-skeleton, commit 4e118d4 — stub modules + skip-marked named acceptance tests with final signatures, bodies unwritten. Implementing a bead = replace its NotImplementedError bodies + unskip its test section; suite stays green throughout. Per-bead file map in each child's notes and SIMPLIFY.md header.

title: T_supp is a synced tree: second root per ws; sync walk reconciles it
description: DELETION_CLOSURE.md §3. Make T_supp a first-class SYNCED structure (second root per workspace alongside T_fact), reconciled by the ordinary sync walk (walk.py / RBSR). Pulling a differing T_supp leaf pulls the co-resident deletion+targets, so out-of-range facts surface during ORDINARY SYNC — not only at read-time closure. This is the 'we want sync to catch them too' requirement. Leaves reference fact bodies by hash (dedup with T_fact); only index nodes are extra (~x2).
notes:
Q5: instantiate the ONE engine (808.2 tree.py, key from shape.py) — hoisting comes for free; T_fact and T_supp reference one shared content-addressed closure pool. Sequencing hazard (SIMPLIFY §3): don't fork the tree layer against 808/jbg.
Production T_supp should instantiate the engine, not the binary prototype jbg.1 replaces: shape.supp_shape() skeleton on branch simplify-skeleton (SIMPLIFY.md §3).

title: Suppression closure edge in the kernel (resolve_supp), validity-independent
description: DELETION_CLOSURE.md §3/§3a. Give the kernel a suppression closure edge: for a fact with a suppression key, resolve the head of its K-group in T_supp; a deletion marker there means the deletion is part of that fact's closure and rides along. This is 'the kernel has to check the tree to know the closure' — but as a CLOSURE edge, NOT a validity input: the fact stays valid, only flagged suppressed, so validity stays globals-blind and parallel drain stays safe. Mirrors resolve_deps. Concurrency needs NO write-time match: T_supp is a CvRDT, concurrent deletion+target writes converge (two-root merge = set union); the only cost is latency-to-visibility (self-healing staleness), not a data race.
notes: Q1/Q3: resolve_supp is a mask-after-judgment closure edge; it fires at MERGE and SERVE (per suppression-participant), NOT at projection. It WRITES the discovery as a ±fid delivery-log row (SIMPLIFY §5 log(seq,±fid)); the pump/projection folds the log with ZERO tree walking. S never lives in app.db (lives in T_supp/root). Cost O(S·log N) at ingest, monotone, paid once.

title: Review removal and revocation against the global suppression match tree
description: Review poc-16's identity removal, device revocation, admin delegation, and ephemeral mint rules in light of DELETION_CLOSURE.md's global suppression/death-key match tree. Determine whether signer or authority-path revocation is a suppression predicate, how the suppression treap surfaces affected out-of-range authority facts, and how forward/future suppression composes with request evaluation without reintroducing database-dependent or arrival-order-dependent validity.
acceptance_criteria: Produce an explicit matrix for direct user authorship, bearer descendants, device descendants, delegated admins, relayed facts, past facts, and future facts; map each verdict to stable validation, suppression closure/projection, or the mint/transport gate; identify required deathkey/suppkey extraction and closure dependencies; update the plan of record and unblock poc-16-gxz with a testable implementation boundary.

title: Close the revocation relay gap for globals-blind durable facts
description: An active workspace member can relay a closed pile signed by an evicted identity because the sync grant authenticates only the relay and durable drain intentionally ignores removal globals. The current chained-auth fix prevents an evicted issuer from laundering a mint through a newly delegated user/device closure, but it does not stop an already-active colluder from transporting the evicted key's future messages, admin grants, or evictions. Preserve the current branch's stable-validation/history-independence constraints; investigate and choose the enforcement seam rather than patching it opportunistically.
acceptance_criteria: Add a realistic regression that demonstrates relay by a distinct active member; specify direct authorship and delegated user/device/admin behavior after removal; reject post-removal authority at a protocol seam that remains arrival-order-independent and convergent; cover the chosen behavior in black-box multi-peer tests and document the token/drain threat model.

title: PROOF: surface out-of-range victims by treap traversal only, zero SQL
description: DELETION_CLOSURE.md §5 — the centerpiece. Synthetic seed with chan=X victims placed OUTSIDE range Q + a delete D inside Q. (1) closure_sync(Q) on T_fact yields D but MISSES out-of-range victims (surface the bug). (2) supp_walk(T_supp, prefix=chan=X) surfaces them. Assert: (a) surfaced==true chan=X set (ground truth from seed); (b) treap node fetches only — instrumented counting store, ZERO idx/SQL calls, fetch count O(matches+depth) not O(M); (c) project(closure) suppresses every chan=X fact in- and out-of-range; (d) shuffled build ⇒ byte-identical T_supp root. Mirrors bench/bench_sync.py + hoist prototype.

title: Surfacing pass close_deletions: one-sided RBSR range walk per death key
description: DELETION_CLOSURE.md §2. close_deletions(closure): for each death key present among validated deletions, supp_walk(T_supp, prefix=K) — a pruned one-sided RBSR range walk (same machinery as walk.py) — and merge ALL matches (incl. out-of-range) into the closure. Cost O(matches+depth), not O(set). Returns a deletion-closed set.
notes: REFINED: resolved as a CLOSURE EDGE at three call sites (sync/kernel/projection), not a one-off pass. Two directions: target->deletion = single head-of-group leaf check (N:1, projection-critical); deletion->targets = range scan (1:N, the out-of-range proof). See DELETION_CLOSURE.md §3.

title: Pass placement: wire close_deletions into closure_sync (after dep-closure, before project)
description: DELETION_CLOSURE.md §2 ('when should the pass be'). Run on the VALIDATED, dep-closed set: after the primary closure walk, before materialize/project. Keeps persistent-validity globals-blind (suppression = projection-time verdict, never a validation input); project must never surface a now-suppressed fact. No globals CAS on the persistent path.

title: Death-key extraction from the clear envelope (is_deletion / deathkey / suppkey)
description: DELETION_CLOSURE.md §1/§6. Define the suppression attribute (death-key domain, start with one: chan). Extract it from the CLEAR ENVELOPE (like dep-refs) so T_supp builds without decrypting bodies — confirm envelope-visible or add an envelope offer. Provide is_deletion(f), deathkey(f), and suppkey(f) = the T_supp key component. Phase 0: everything else keys off this.
close_reason: Implemented envelope-only channel suppression/death keys with canonical marker extraction, content-family integration, malformed/bypass coverage, and an explicit safe wire-shape cutover; Codex and Claude Fable approved; full suite 96 passed, 29 skipped.

title: Suppression-key treap T_supp (key = suppkey || ts:fid; reuse treap.build/update)
description: DELETION_CLOSURE.md §1. Second content-addressed Merkle treap over the SAME fact set, key = suppkey||ts:fid, so all facts sharing a death key sort contiguously (the deletion + its N victims). Pure function of the set; built/maintained by the EXISTING treap.build/treap.update (blind incremental = the 'update the tree on new suppression keys' requirement). Facts with no suppression attribute are absent.
notes:
REFINED (concurrency turn): T_supp is a SYNCED tree (second root per ws), NOT locally derived — syncing the index is how out-of-range facts surface. Tag-ordered key: suppkey||tag||ts:fid, deletions tag=0 (sort to group head), targets tag=1. See DELETION_CLOSURE.md §3.
Q4/Q5 (2026-07-24): T_supp leaves are CLOSED piles — each deletion rides with its OWN validity closure (admin/authority chain, signatures); only valid deletions enter S (S(D)=targets of *valid* suppression facts). That closure is SHARED (one admin deletes many channels) so ρ≈3x leaf-dup hits T_supp too — production T_supp must ride the HOISTING engine (808.2 tree.py / jbg.1 fat nodes), NOT the flat per-leaf-close prototype, and shares ONE content-addressed hoisted closure pool with T_fact (only index nodes extra, ~x2). The yez.6 proof may use the prototype; production must not. See DELETION_CLOSURE.md §3b + SIMPLIFY.md §3.

title: Global 1:N deletion closure — suppression-key treap (surface out-of-range victims, no DB)
description: Resolve the multi-target-deletion Open Question in DESIGN.md by making the 1:N (channel/predicate) deletion join a SECOND closure augmentation: a range walk in a second content-addressed treap (T_supp) keyed by the suppression/death key, structurally identical to the dep-ref closure (P3) but keyed by a predicate attribute instead of a backward hash pointer. Removes the 'singleton serial pass / full state awareness' requirement DESIGN.md currently states for multi-target deletion. Plan of record: DELETION_CLOSURE.md. Centerpiece: a proof (bench/property test) that surfaces out-of-range deletion-offering facts into the closure by treap traversal alone, zero SQL.
design: See DELETION_CLOSURE.md. Backward/out-of-range victims closed by the T_supp range walk; forward/future victims closed by the globals suppress-if set (existing globals-blind fold). Suppression stays a projection-time verdict, so parallel drain and the globals-blind rule are untouched. Composes with the non-serialized/CvRDT FaaS epic: T_supp is another state-based-CRDT tree.

title: SEC/CvRDT property test (concurrent writers converge)
description: Prove the coordination-free guarantee: concurrent writers folding disjoint/overlapping piles converge to a BIT-IDENTICAL root; two-root merge = fold of the union; non-serialized writes lose no data (roots never clobber piles).

title: Incremental fold on upload + two-root merge O(diff)
description: Event-driven incremental fold: a new pile folds in O(pile + log N) via path-copy, O(log N) memory. Two roots merge to root(A union B) in O(diff) via the RBSR descent (tree-join). No re-fold from scratch.

title: Store trait: S3 + R2 drivers (strong RAW + conditional writes)
description: One store trait over S3 and R2: strong read-after-write + single-key CAS (S3 If-Match / R2 onlyIf), presigned or GET serving, LIST for the pile set. Never use an eventually-consistent KV for root. Foundational for the CF runtime.

title: Land FaaS concurrency + Cloudflare Workers deployment (coordination-free)
description: Land the coordination-free FaaS / CF Workers design goals from DESIGN.md sec Concurrency & FaaS and WORKSPACES.md sec 9: content-addressed CRDT with Strong Eventual Consistency, non-serialized (no lease by default), fat B-tree MST/prolly nodes (no manifest), one-sided RBSR against a dumb store, generational GC, Workers-exclusive deployment.

title: Fat B-tree Merkle nodes (drop the flat manifest)
description: DESIGN.md sec Concurrency & FaaS. Move the layout from a binary treap + flat manifest to fat B-tree (MST/prolly) nodes: each node carries every child (hash, fingerprint). Self-describing + shallow (~2-3 levels) so no separate manifest object. Foundational for the rest.
notes: Per SIMPLIFY.md §2, execute this bead AS the engine extraction: skeleton tinyp2p/tree.py on branch simplify-skeleton (fat() is this bead's packing; anchor+globals ride tree.Root once the manifest drops). See poc-16-808.2.

title: Precomputed fingerprints + reader-driven pruned walk (GET-only)
description: Bake fingerprints into the immutable nodes so a DUMB store answers a reader-driven fingerprint-pruned walk with only GETs (git dumb-HTTP over a Merkle DAG). Range-read the node fingerprint region to trim bytes.

title: Non-serialized root: append-only roots set + amortized merge (drop the lease)
description: Publish roots into an append-only roots/ set; truth = merge(live roots), never clobbered. Amortize merge/sweep into every fold + authoritative read (deterministic merges dedup by hash, no storm). CAS-pointer (S3 If-Match / R2 onlyIf) and blind-LWW+sweep as variants. Remove the single-writer lease as the default; lease/DO becomes a per-workspace opt-in.

title: Update MULTILEVEL_PILE.md A.5 with the deep-chain result

close_reason: Replaced the star caveat with 49,999-fact star/wide/random/chain histograms and tax tables, plus shallow/deep and multi-device verdicts.

Confirm the acceptance criteria and deliver the one-paragraph verdict: does aligning key order to the real delegation tree turn the range-sync tax from O(members) into O(depth), and does it matter for the realistic shallow-wide shape or only the adversarial deep one?

Shapes star/wide/random/chain; record the realized depth histogram (min/median/max hops to root). Author messages as today. Realism: real graphs are shallow-and-wide, so measure all shapes and do not report only the deep number.

Hypothesis: deleg tax ~ 4 x depth(subtree), path-length-bounded not N-bounded; deleg beats author/ts on the deep shape and reproduces A.5 on the star. Add a depth column.

description: CHAINED_AUTH_PLAN.md sec 7.3. bench_sync catchup/bidi and check_leaves (leaves-are-piles) must still pass on the chained seed: every published leaf carries its full delegation closure. Use it as an oracle.
close_reason: All four chained shapes pass check_leaves, fresh catchup, and bidirectional reconciliation; realistic guard tests added and full suite passes.

description: See CHAINED_AUTH_PLAN.md (plan) and WORKSPACES.md (settled model). Unlock deep delegation via member-can-invite, build chained seeds, measure the hoisting key-order tax by depth, and close the depth-1 star caveat in MULTILEVEL_PILE.md A.5. Uses poc-13 naming.

Touches every import plus tests/benches (tests/util.py, bench_sync.py, bench_order.py, cli.py, cmds.py, content/message.py). One green commit before any semantic change. Unit test: a member-signed invite validates, a non-member-signed one is rejected. This one line is the whole depth mechanism, and per WORKSPACES.md the same primitive powers cross-device mirroring and infra.

title: Keep changed-fid projection filtering linear
description: Device reconciliation tests membership in merge's changed-fid list for every closure-expanded valid, making bulk ingest O(U*V). Normalize changed IDs to a set once at the projection boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Changed-fid filtering uses set-like membership and a realistic bulk regression demonstrates it does not perform list membership per valid.
close_reason: Projection boundary normalizes changed ids to a frozenset once; bulk closure-replay regression rejects linear list membership.

title: Avoid replay-driven full device roster projection
description: Reviewed closure piles replay already-known device facts on every device-authored write. device.reconcile sees those replayed device_key offers and deletes/reinserts the full workspace device roster even though no canonical winner changed, making ordinary writes O(total devices).
acceptance_criteria: Materialize/reconcile only newly admitted facts unless canonical pruning/restoration requires a full reprojection; add a realistic device-authored ordinary-write regression proving the roster is not rebuilt; preserve winner-switch reprojection and pass the full suite.
close_reason: Device reconciliation now considers only newly admitted facts during ordinary turns and uses the full active set only for canonical reprojection; device-authored writes no longer rebuild the roster and winner-switch tests remain green.

title: Keep direct device grants deterministic across proof-winner changes
description: A direct grant that inherits its current canonical device provider's timestamp changes fid if an equal-valid provider later becomes canonical. A retry then misses the exact fact and fails as already enrolled, violating deterministic lost-response and reconcile retries.
acceptance_criteria: Derive the mandatory Fact timestamp from immutable workspace/logical-cell input without scanning for an existing logical grant; preserve the rule that timestamps carry no causal weight; add a restart retry and a canonical-provider-switch retry regression.
close_reason: Direct grants derive their required timestamp from the immutable workspace anchor, never a mutable proof winner or logical-cell scan; restart and provider-switch retry regressions pass.

title: Docs foldback: DESIGN.md engine/mint/node-state; mark prototypes absorbed

For a linearizable 'is X deleted?' that must never return a stale-live answer, add an OPT-IN authoritative mode on the per-workspace Durable-Object / CAS lease (the FaaS epic's opt-in path) — optimistic retry / lease live HERE ONLY, never in the default. Build the read-mode selector. Default lock/queue is rejected (reintroduces the per-ws serialization bottleneck the FaaS epic removed).

description: DELETION_CLOSURE.md §5.6. Vary M and out-of-range fraction; report rounds/node-fetches/bytes for the surfacing walk vs a naive pull-the-whole-set baseline; show cost tracks match-count not set size; report T_supp overhead (~x2 index nodes; leaves dedup by content).

title: OPTIONAL hot-death-key globals cache (subsumed by T_supp head-check)
description: DELETION_CLOSURE.md §3. The future half: a validated death key rides the globals slot (suppress-if set), so incoming facts matching K are suppressed at drain by the existing globals-blind fold — no walk. T_supp closes the past, globals close the future.
notes: SUPERSEDED for correctness by the T_supp head-of-group check, which closes the FUTURE direction too (a future target lands in the K-group; next projection sees the head marker). Keep the globals suppress-if slot ONLY as an optional cache for hot death keys; NOT required for correctness. See DELETION_CLOSURE.md §3.

title: Cloudflare Workers runtime + sizing conformance
description: Run the engine on CF Workers exclusively: R2 store, fold triggered by R2 event notifications to Queues, cold rebuild via a Durable Object alarm loop or copy-the-tree. Conformance: O(log N) mem / O(ms) incremental CPU within 128MB/30s (5min), pile parses in a few MB, Workers-exclusive (no heavy tier).

title: Generational GC (Merkle reachability over a grace window)
description: Reclaim only objects no root within a grace window reaches (git-gc + reflog window). The folder that path-copies stamps superseded nodes with a grace expiry; reclamation lazy, never on the correctness path.

title: Reader modes: fast vs authoritative; RYW/monotonic/causal
description: One read primitive (walk store, pruned by fingerprint, scoped by range). Fast = walk a recent root (may lag). Authoritative = reconcile (root-vs-LIST diff or peer fingerprint diff); empty-prior = full catch-up. RYW client-side (fold own pile after PUT); monotonic reads via a watermark (merge, never replace); causal free from dep-closure.
